verdict: Push-training-dose is NOT the lever that saves M4 turn-tracking. Cutting training push exposure from pushcont1's 1.0 to 0.25 (same base 10-25N force, same fault-first init) barely moves tip error: hand-run eval_yaw (hazards zeroed) reads tip-left/right 0.2642/0.2690 vs pushcont1's own 0.2727/0.3029 -- inside single-eval noise of 'unchanged', nowhere near the pre-registered PASS-clean bar (both <=0.20-0.25) and matching the gate's own pre-registered FLAT branch, not PARTIAL. Own-cfg DR-0 walk floor holds (gait_valid 11/12 det+sto, matches parent's 11/12 exactly, 0 terminations, one legit carried leg [4], clean six-leg video). Worse: the paired eval_amp_m5 push section (eval-time forced ext_push_prob=1.0, per the gate's own 'confirm push-recovery survives the lower dose' instruction) shows push-recovery competence did NOT survive -- sto terminations under forced push jumped 2 (pushcont1) -> 5 (this run), busting the section's own cap of <=3, even though gait_valid stayed fine (12/12). So the dose cut buys no turn-tracking headroom and actively costs push robustness on the one axis it was supposed to protect -- the income competition between yaw-tracking and push-survival is structural, not proportional to training exposure fraction. Training reward rose all run (39/101/173/203 per quarter) but this is a pre-registered behavioral grid, not an undertrained lineage -- the FLAT branch's own prescription is to escalate to the deferred hold/forward repricing build, not to relaunch more dose points on this substrate. Evidence: logs/ckpt_eval/cw_amp_m4_turnfault_seq1_pushdose025_{gate,m5}/, cf. cw_amp_m4_turnfault_seq1_{,pushcont1_}m5/m5_verdict.json.

verdict: Result: dose-curve TURNOVER, the pre-registered branch -- pushing dedicated turn-episode exposure from 0.5 (tipfrac05, champion) to 0.7 does NOT further improve turn tracking, it REGRESSES it, and also erodes general walk safety. Evidence (eval_amp_m5 formal verdict, m5_pass=false; walk=false yaw=false push=true fault=true): yaw section tip-left/right err 0.2359/0.2252 (up from tipfrac05's bar-clean 0.162/0.184 -- back to the tipfrac02/03 in-band-not-clean band, i.e. MORE turn-exposure made tip-tracking WORSE, not better). Walk section fails on BOTH counts: n_translating collapsed to 2/12 (0/6 det, 2/6 sto) at this dose -- too few translating episodes even to compute a det median (harness sampling gap at high turn-frac, a real methodology note for future high-dose arms) -- and the 2 translating episodes that DID land both exceed the slip bar (4.03/4.30 > 3.5, sto_slip_med 4.168). Own-cfg DR-0 gate also regresses vs tipfrac05's clean 12/12: gait_valid 10/12 with TWO video-confirmed tilt_roll falls (roll peak 35.0deg det, 34.6deg sto) plus 2 sacrificed-leg sto episodes -- a real safety-margin cost from the dose alone (same seed=7 as the champion, so this is NOT the seed-lottery finding from -s3, it's an independent dose-driven regression). Fault section is the one axis that holds/slightly improves (10/12 gv, meets bar, vs tipfrac05's 9/12) -- not enough to offset the yaw+walk+safety regression. CONCLUSION: the turn-exposure dose curve peaks at 0.5 and turns over by 0.7; tipfrac05 (seed7) remains the sole M5-candidate champion. Grid CLOSED (0.2/0.3/0.5/0.7 all read): 0.5 is confirmed the sweet spot, not merely the largest dose tried. Next: no further dose arms on this lever; the two already-flagged prerequisites (hold/forward income repricing for budget-stability, seed-safety-variance root cause) remain the funded path to an M5-candidate promotion, both already DIG-IN-flagged and in progress on a concurrent cycle (uncommitted walk_kernel_yaw_ema work in tree at review time) -- left untouched, no duplicate launch.

Isolated m5 walk/push/fault sections all PASS, each a bit better than acq1's own numbers (walk det_slip 2.97 vs acq1's over-bar 3.52; fault det_prog 0.98 vs 0.56, gait_valid unchanged 11/12) -- kernel-EMA is not globally harmful, it specifically fails to rescue (and mildly worsens) the yaw-tracking axis it targets. Root cause (already diagnosed, unbuilt): the EMA kernels never reset on a goal.vx_ref/wz_ref command change, so a policy trained under them learns to damp body dynamics for ~tau after any translation-heavy segment ends, which costs nothing in ordinary training (stress_mix resamples) but directly suppresses the abrupt heading-authority eval_amp_m5's tip-left/right segments (which immediately follow arc-max turns) are timed to measure. CLOSES the kernel-EMA question at n=5 arms (kernelema1, yawonly, velonly2, acq-kernelema, this run) across both fresh-retrain and fixed-basin-continuation regimes: naive kernel-EMA repricing does not rescue AMP M4 turn-tracking in either regime. verdict: Doubling the slip charge to 12x-per-excess did not move slip at all — the policy simply pays the fine and keeps skating, so additive slip pricing at the aggressive dose is NOT the lever. Evidence: eval_amp_m5 walk section det slip med 3.79 vs bar 3.5 and vs parent pushcal518 3.67 (family band 3.62-3.82 — unmoved; the gate's pre-registered FAIL branch). The charge demonstrably fired in training: env/reward_loadslip_excess ~-0.98/tick at end (exactly the predicted ~1/tick vs ~3/tick walk income), yet training walk_loadslip_ratio only edged ~3.6->3.50 and reward still rose (quarters 33.8->156.4) — the reward optimum sits at slip ~3.5-3.8 even after paying the charge. NOT over-charged: safety and gait fully held — own-cfg DR-0 gate 0/12 raw falls (0 terms det+sto; family-signature caveats only: 1 sto sacrificed-leg ep, 2 near-stationary sto eps), m5 walk gait_valid 12/12 with det prog med 1.03, video shows clean upright tripod cycling, no park/suicide farming; yaw tips 0.2234/0.2413 within the <=0.25 no-regress leg (still over the 0.20 m5 bar, unchanged vs family). Why: the marginal cost of slipping less exceeds 1/tick — slip ~3.6 is structurally coupled to how this gait produces progress (stance micro-skate), so price nudges cannot buy it down; that is a mechanism problem, not a dose problem. Hardware-ready: no (walk slip above M5 bar). Next: per the pre-registered joint rule, if slipexcess6 (concurrent cycle) also fails to move slip, additive pricing is refuted for this axis and the next lever is the partial-strength loadslip income gate; this higher-dose zero-movement result already makes that outcome near-certain.

hypothesis: Plain English: we are deciding whether the gait found by direct CPG search is as good a style example for AMP training as the hand-scripted teacher; the first A/B at 2M showed the CPG library walking but ~15-20% softer on det margins (prog 0.99 vs 1.16, slip 2.46 vs 1.88, fwd 0.59 vs 0.69m) -- this arm re-runs the SAME cpgv1 recipe at 3x budget (6M, only --steps changed) with a teacher_v2 twin at matched budget, to tell whether that det gap is a fixed property of the style target or an early-training transient. Prediction-if-true (gap is transient): cpgv1-6m closes to parity with teacher-6m (det prog >=0.95x of the twin, det slip <=1.15x, fwd within 0.1m). Prediction-if-false (gap is real): gap persists or widens at matched budget -> teacher_v2 confirmed the better style source; adoption fork closes with no swap, cpg_v1 stays a diversity resource. Strongest alternative: 6M of this fragile minimal-reward discovery recipe degrades BOTH arms (crouch collapse or gait_valid loss) -- then budget, not library, dominates and the 2M reads stand as the honest comparison.

Evidence (eval_amp_m5 walk+yaw own-cfg, this dig-in cycle): tip_left_err 0.1778 (parent pushcal518 0.2157, -0.038, CLEARS the 0.20 bar), tip_right_err 0.2151 (parent 0.2351, -0.020, just misses), walk det slip med 3.919 vs parent 3.67 (+0.25 REGRESSION past the +-0.15 band, sto slip 4.85), 0 terms / gait_valid 12/12 / 0 yaw falls. Training telemetry matches: walk_yaw_err last10 0.257 vs priced arms' 0.256 (raw exposure unchanged; the eval-side tip gain is the discriminator pressure coming OFF at the achieved-rate margin). ROOT CAUSE, measured this cycle by direct probe of the scripted teacher: the untrimmed tripod gait ACHIEVES only 0.134-0.144 rad/s at commanded 0.25-0.30 (ratio 0.48-0.54 - exactly the price-invariant ~0.5 ratio every tipfrac05 policy is pinned at), saturating ~0.15-0.16 at any commanded omega because foot sweep per stride is geometry-capped; teacher_v2's turn demos therefore EMBODY ~0.134 rad/s while labeled 0.25, and the discriminator (obs_style includes base_angular_velocity, unconditioned on command) punishes any rotation faster than the demos. Next: keep AMP on and fix the demos - teacher_v3.npz built+snapshotted this cycle (turn clips at stride_scale 1.4/period_scale 1.2 = measured 0.174 rad/s, +30% demo ceiling, slip/m 1.26, non-turn clips bit-exact); arm -turnlib3 launches on it. Slip axis gets the full-strength recalibrated loadslip income gate (-loadgate45) since AMP-off made slip worse and additive pricing is refuted.

Evidence (matched 2M budget vs matched parent pushcal518): m5 walk det slip med 4.3685 vs parent 3.67 (bar 3.5; seed-noise band ~±0.15-0.2 per the tipspawn 3-seed grid) — the only slip-lever arm that actively REGRESSED walk slip; stance-drag probe median 15.84mm vs matched control 14.03 (the anneal rung reads 9.55 for scale); fault section regressed to gait_valid 10/12 with 2 sacrificed legs [2,5] (bar >=10 with <=1); tip_right 0.2646 vs parent 0.2351. The one predicted bright spot did land: tip_left 0.1936 (parent 0.2157) — first member of this family to clear the strict 0.20 line on the ccw side, exactly the cpg_v1 ccw-favorable turn asymmetry the hypothesis named — but the gate's FAIL clause (any fault regression) overrides the tip PARTIAL clause. Safety preserved: 0/12 falls, walk gait_valid 12/12, clean upright six-leg det strips. Reward-vs-eval per the binding triage rule: training reward rose smoothly 42->248 while every gate axis regressed vs the matched control at the same budget — this is the prediction-if-false mechanism confirmed (the discriminator's obs_style features — joint pos/vel, base angvel, foot pos — do not transmit the clips' recorded ground-contact slip, so imitating low-slip demos does not inherit low slip), plus the named strongest-alternative (anchor swap destabilizes the converged basin) visible on the fault axis. NOT a continue case: the question was mechanism-vs-matched-control, answered cleanly. Next per pre-registration: demo-anchor fork CLOSED; escalate the q_20260823T0700Z slip-bar amendment (option (a): score m5 walk slip on translating segments only — the metric's median episode is turn-in-place, n_translating 3/12, same defect class the cpg track already fixed in its own scorer 08-22); yaw structural lever continues in cmdcond1 (training) and wzmask1 (triaged this cycle).

hypothesis: Plain English: the AMP discriminator has been blind to WHAT ROTATION RATE WAS COMMANDED the whole time -- it only ever sees the robot's raw body spin, so any policy that turns faster than the teacher's own demo clips (which embody ~0.13-0.18 rad/s no matter what label they carry) reads as 'moving unlike the teacher' and gets docked, capping turn-in-place tracking. Four DIFFERENT mechanism classes already failed to fix this on the pushcal518 lineage: pricing the turn income harder (k_yaw_prog 1x/2x/3x), widening the demo ceiling itself (teacher_v3, +30% measured wz), removing the style term entirely (noamp1, which also broke slip), and reset-densifying into more turn states (tipspawn1b/tipspawn3). This arm is the first STRUCTURAL fix: append the LIVE commanded (vx_ref, vy_ref, wz_ref) to the discriminator's 60-dim obs_style (-> 63-dim, goal.amp_style_cmd_cond=1, new code this cycle, tests green) and rebuild the motion library the SAME way (teacher_v2_cmdcond.npz -- bit-identical to teacher_v2.npz on all 45 clips' first 60 dims and slip/m, verified; only the command tail is new) so the discriminator can finally judge 'does this look like the teacher's motion GIVEN what was asked for' instead of penalizing high wz outright. Single coupled lever vs pushcal518 (flag + matching-dim library must change together or it's a shape-mismatch crash by design, not two independent variables). Prediction-if-true: yaw tip_left/right_err move meaningfully toward or under the 0.20 bar (>=0.03 improvement on the worse side, mirroring the noamp1/pricing-grid noise band already measured at seed-to-seed std ~0.02) without a new fall/fault regression. Prediction-if-false: tips stay within the family's own measured seed-noise band (tipspawn1b-recipe reads at fixed seeds 11/13/17 span tip_left 0.19-0.24, tip_right 0.21-0.26, i.e. +-0.03) -- command-conditioning doesn't help either, closing structural obs-space fixes and leaving only the 0.20 bar amendment (q_20260823T0130Z) as an option. Strongest alternative: the discriminator's LS-GAN dynamics don't actually use the new tail dims meaningfully (co-training absorbs them as noise) -- watch amp/d_real vs amp/d_fake and amp/style_reward_mean stay healthy (not saturated, not collapsed) as a mechanism-health check independent of the behavior bars.
gate: eval_amp_m5 full suite (walk/yaw/push/fault) + weight-movement precheck vs turnfault_seq1 (non-log_std tensors must differ, this run really trained) + discriminator health (amp/d_real vs amp/d_fake stay separated, not saturated/collapsed). PASS = 0/12 raw falls AND walk gait_valid 12/12 AND tip_left_err<=0.20 AND tip_right_err<=0.20 AND walk det_slip_med within 0.5 of pushcal518's own 3.67 (no new slip regression) AND fault gait_valid>=10. PARTIAL = at least one tip clears 0.20 or both move >=0.03 toward it with 0 new falls, but the other or slip does not fully clear -- mechanism real, worth an acquisition-budget continuation or composing with the CPG-demo-swap arm (cpgdemo1, concurrent). FAIL = both tips land within the family's own +-0.03 seed-noise band of pushcal518's 0.2157/0.2351 (i.e. no clear improvement beyond noise) -- command-conditioning refuted, close structural-fix search on the discriminator obs side. Falls/fault regression override any tip improvement to FAIL regardless of tip numbers (safety first).

verdict: The from-scratch rung-1 policy never tried to walk: it froze into a tilt-safe splayed crouch for the whole 2M steps, and the dig-in shows exactly why the pricing makes that rational. OBSERVATIONS: W&B components (wandbdump, 287 rows): env/reward_walk_prog is identically 0.0 for the ENTIRE run (not one step of commanded progress ever sampled); step-event rate flat at ~0.02/step from 0.2M to 2M (zero learning progress on the task axis); ep_len grows 16->490 while per-step reward falls +2.6 -> -4.7 (dominated by loadslip charge -3.95, height -0.77, heading -0.5); tilt terminations are optimized away early (r_term -> 0). The 'collapsing' ep_rew_mean (-100/-541/-1169/-1988 by quarter) is an undiscounted-logging artifact: longer survival x negative per-step rate; with truncation bootstrapping, freeze's discounted value (~-4.7/(1-gamma) ~ -470) rationally beats exploratory falling (-1200 terminal). PPO optimized its objective correctly; the objective makes freezing the reachable optimum. INTERPRETATION (root cause, behavior <- incentive <- pricing <- no sim defect): every v2e income channel requires competent locomotion BEFORE it pays (k_step_event needs a >=10mm ALONG-COMMAND swing; freeprog needs real command-direction velocity), so from random init the only live gradients are dense penalties, and the loadslip travel-floor (0.03m) charges any non-traveling shuffle escalatingly (ls_ratio 1.65->23) — exploration toward stepping must first climb UP the penalty gradient through tilt-risky motion. The bank's stall(-31.5) > park(-352) exit exists on paper but is unreachable by local policy-gradient steps. The WALKCURR_PF bank could never see this: it ranks scripted lifetime trajectories, not reachability from random init. VERDICT: FAIL (exploration-unsafe pricing confirmed, STATUS working theory refined — it is not term_penalty=1200 alone, it is zero reachable income). hardware-ready: no (does not walk at all). HYPOTHESIS STATUS: refuted as launched; fix armed this cycle — reward.k_walk_swing=1.0 (existing mechanism, pays ANY completed >=15mm swing, the only income random flail can reach), bank-extended with the pre-registered shuffle farming attack and PROVEN green on both new stacks (gait +409.9 > stall -21.5 > park -351.7 > shuffle -430 NEGATIVE > sideways -534.5 > reverse -675.2 > topple/skate floor; swingterm800 keeps topple -764 < reverse by 89): launching cw-walkcurr-pf-fwd2-swing (single lever) and cw-walkcurr-pf-fwd2-swingterm800 (+ catastrophe relief) as the rung-1 discovery batch.

hypothesis: Plain English: hiding only the yaw-rate sensor from the AMP style critic (wzmask1) did nothing, so this last gyro-channel arm hides the robot's ENTIRE body-rotation sense (gyro x/y/z, obs_style dims 36-38) from the discriminator to test whether ANY direct rotation-rate channel is what suppresses turning speed. Pre-registered as wzmask1's single FAIL-branch follow-up. Single lever vs pushcal518 (same seed 7, 2M): --amp-style-mask-dims 38 -> 36,37,38; default-off masking mechanism already tested (test_amp_style_mask.py 6/6). Prediction-if-true: m5 yaw tips move >=0.03 toward 0.20 (noamp1 read 0.1778/0.2151) with walk det_slip_med within the family band (3.55-3.85). Prediction-if-false: tips unmoved (±0.02 of parent 0.2157/0.2351) — the discriminator reads rotation speed off joint_vel/foot-trajectory dims, the gyro-channel hypothesis CLOSES for good, and the yaw axis rests on cmdcond1's command-conditioning or the stance-geometry/turn-curriculum fork. Strongest alternative: masking roll/pitch rates (36/37) also degrades the style term's stabilizing pressure and costs fault/push robustness or slip — reproducing a partial noamp1 trade.

verdict: Slowing the gait metronome from 1.33 Hz to 0.5 Hz is the FIRST lever in eight mechanism classes that actually teaches the robot to turn in place at the graded rate -- and it fixes slip too, but it halves forward walking speed. Evidence (m5 suite + walk-per-mode-24 re-read, n_translating=28): yaw tips 0.1488/0.1557 vs parent 0.2157/0.2351 (improve 0.067/0.079, BOTH sides clear the strict 0.20 M5 bar for the first time on this lineage; yaw section PASS); walk det_slip_med 2.443 -- best ever on this lineage (family band 3.47-3.83, bar 3.5), gait_valid 48/48, 0 terms; fault 11/12 gv (leg 5 sacrificed, family range), push 12/12 gv with 1 det term (bar <=2). BUT walk det_prog_med 0.52 vs family ~0.94 and m5 bar 0.75 -- achieved speed ~0.04 m/s vs 0.08 commanded, a cost the pre-registered gate did not price, so PARTIAL not PASS (gate note: slip landed BELOW the literal 3.2-4.0 band -- on the good side; judged as improvement per the band's anti-regression intent). Why: cadence was the binding constraint on yaw-per-stride, exactly as the CPG 0.5Hz/13-15deg measurement predicted; but 2M steps at 0.5 Hz has not yet grown strides enough to hold 0.08 m/s translation. Next: cadence dose sweep 0.7/0.9/1.1 (find the point where tips stay <=0.20 and prog recovers >=0.75) + continue this arm +4M (reward still rising 43.5->216.5 by quarters; 08-21 ruling) to test if stride growth recovers prog at 0.5 Hz. Video: walk det strips clean six-leg cycling, upright, no flag leg.

Strongest alternative: retraining against a different discriminator target destabilizes the basin (falls/fault regressions) independent of the cadence question -- FAIL branches on safety are judged separately from tips-unmoved.

hypothesis: Plain English: fwd1-fwd5 (8 arms total) all froze in an identical static crouch no matter how the reward charges were priced/ramped, and a cheap W&B-history read (no GPU) confirmed WHY across 3 of those arms: train/clip_fraction collapses to EXACTLY 0 within the first third of every 2M-step run and never recovers -- PPO's per-step i.i.d. Gaussian action noise apparently never produces a rollout with real net forward displacement to reinforce (fresh init/entropy-coef arms already ruled out noise MAGNITUDE; this tests noise STRUCTURE instead). hypothesis: Plain English: the robot never learns to walk because PPO's own optimizer is crushing its learning signal -- the reward numbers are simply too BIG, so this arm shrinks every reward gain 10x without changing what the reward prefers. Dig-in evidence (all 8 FAILed rung-1 arms, cached W&B): train/clip_fraction hits EXACTLY 0 by 10-38% of every run, approx_kl ~3e-5, policy std frozen at its init 0.3685, while train/value_loss sits at 400-2000+ (returns are |1000s|-scale under v2e pricing). SB3 clips the GLOBAL grad norm (max_grad_norm=0.5) over policy+value params in ONE optimizer, so the value head's huge gradients rescale the policy/log_std/entropy gradients toward zero -- explaining why pricing, init-noise (logstd0 collapsed FASTEST), and 10x-entropy (std moved only 0.369->0.376 in 2M) all failed identically. SB3 normalizes advantages per minibatch, so a global gain scale leaves the policy gradient invariant and shrinks ONLY the value gradient: the crush lifts, nothing about the incentive ordering changes. verdict: FAIL - the operator's full-circle V6 ladder run finished its whole 40M budget frozen at bucket b1 (front45_20s) and every landed eval fails. Plain words: the robot never learned to actually STOP when told to, so the curriculum never let it try sideways or backwards walking, and 40M steps of hammering one 20s front-cone bucket made the base gait WORSE than its parent. Evidence: (1) promotion b0->b1 at 540k, then b1 cert FAILED its stop check on all ~79 remaining rounds - walkcurr/b1_front45_20s/stop_speed_m_s flat in [0.036,0.047] vs the 0.015 cert bar, reward converged early (quarters 913.9/1062.0/1054.1/1042.6) so per the 08-21 ruling this is misalignment, not undertraining; (2) joygate FAIL: 8 falls/48 (5 at DR-0!), dir_err 40.69>40, gait_valid 0.917 - parent lineage passed this gate 0 falls; (3) own-DR walk FAIL: det 1/6 over_current termination, gait_valid 3/6 det, dir_err med 42.1. ROOT CAUSE (corrects the earlier triage note): k_walk_freeprog was NEVER active in this run (default 0.0, not in the cfg-set list; no freeprog keys in W&B) - the real defect is that NOTHING in this cfg prices stop-command speed except the Gaussian velocity kernel, whose optimum-vs-creep margin is shallow (still 2.0/tick vs 0.04-creep 1.45/tick, +0.55/tick) while prog-gate/course/park-duty/step/drag are all guarded by s_ref>1e-3 and pay/charge NOTHING on stop ticks. The cert bar (mean stop-tick speed<=0.015 incl. decel transient) has no matching reward term, so PPO's converged optimum is the observed ~0.04 creep. verdict: Confound-fix arm FAILS the rung-1 gate on the SAME underlying trajectory as every prior height-gate arm, even though the fix itself worked mechanically. Evidence: env/reward_park_duty is now nonzero throughout (-0.003 -> -0.011, was EXACTLY 0 all run on hgt2) confirming goal.park_duty_window_s=0.5 does fill before the 2.0s grace and the charge fires as designed. But env/walk_freeprog_score never leaves [-0.11,-0.10] (ends -0.098, no improvement over hgt2/hgt1), env/walk_speed decays 0.10->0.054 m/s, env/height_err_mm climbs monotonically 11->51mm the same way hgt1's did, and clip_fraction dips to near-zero mid-run (2.6e-5) before a partial recovery (0.029) -- reward and eval both non-improving with adequate budget = genuinely stuck, not misaligned, per the 08-21 ruling. Own-cfg gate: 6/6 det + 6/6 sto episodes terminate walk_low_height (the tight 25mm cutoff now firing every time, height_err_end 63-95mm), gait_valid now TRUE with duty spread 0.12-0.84 (no more sacrificed legs, so the tripod-lock escape specifically IS closed) but forward_dist is 0.007-0.03m/25s and slip_per_m 5.8-7.8 -- video (walk_det_0.png) shows a slow progressive splay-and-sink over the episode into a wide low crouch, zero net translation, then the safety cutoff ends it. Why: de-confounding the charge changed WHICH static pose the policy settles into (rigid tripod-lock -> splayed slow-sink) but not WHETHER it settles into one; the underlying survive-motionless-beats-risk-a-fall economics this whole campaign has been probing is untouched by this lever. What's next: read jointly with the pdx15 dose sibling (also FAIL, same signature) -- this closes the park_duty-class charge (any bank-legal dose, confound fixed or not) as a mechanism for unlocking rung-1 discovery. DIG-IN flagged for the next escalation choice (direct minimum-total-foot-contact charge, a new mechanism needing its own scripted twin + bank proof, vs. finally flagging the BC-kickstart last resort to the operator) since every other named lever (RND dose+budget, rung-0 swing-income, GRU, gSDE, rscale dose+continuations, height-gate dose+confound) is now closed.

verdict: The Stage-A slip-diagnostic arm FAILS discovery, and its distinguishing lever -- loosening the safety cutoffs -- made the known belly-sit basin strictly WORSE: the robot now drops flat onto its belly within the first seconds and lies there with five of six feet waving in the air, so the new planted-foot slip charge it was built to measure never even fires (feet that never touch cannot slip). Evidence: reward fell MONOTONICALLY all run (quarters 43.8/38.8/25.7/9.5, end ep_rew_mean -0.03) while height_err climbed 11->111mm, walk_swinging_feet rose 3.1->5.3/6, liftoff_count decayed 0.38->0.10/s, walk_speed 0.10->0.009 m/s, and reward_foot_slip_tangent sat at -0.00007 (unmeasurably small, per the no-contact evasion, NOT because slipping is clean). Own-cfg gate (podeval, watched det strip): det 0/6 gait_valid with ALL SIX legs sacrificed, prog med -0.01, fwd 0.01m, slip/m 7.49, ZERO terminations (the disabled height cutoff lets episodes marinate the full 25s in the absorbing pose); sto slip 19-23/m is just exploration jitter ground-scrubbing. Video: splayed belly-flat collapse by frame 2, zero net motion after. Hardware-ready: no. Reward AND eval both falling with adequate budget = genuine FAIL per the 08-21 ruling, not misaligned-continue. Mechanism reads for the open escalation DIG-IN (pdw05/pdx15): (1) the safety termination was the only pressure bounding time-in-basin -- removing it turned belly-sit into a fully absorbing state that PPO's state distribution slides into even as collected reward falls; any future anti-collapse charge (e.g. the named minimum-total-foot-contact/no-fly charge) must come WITH a termination/hard boundary, never INSTEAD of one, because absorbing states beat prices. (2) The tangent-slip charge is closed as a discovery lever on this rung: it is evadable by zero contact and returns no data in exactly the failure mode that matters. (3) METRIC WARNING: walk_freeprog_score read 'best-ever' (-0.016, monotone toward 0) on this arm purely because EMA speed -> 0 while lying down -- freeprog-toward-zero must never be read as discovery health without a contact/height cross-check. (4) This is now the ~11th independent mechanism (RND doses x3, rung-0 swing income x2+RND, GRU, gSDE, rscale, hgt1/hgt2 terminations, park_duty confound+dose, tangent slip + loosened safety) converging on the same static/collapsed basin from random init -- strengthens the case the escalation cycle weighs for the BC-kickstart last resort vs one final bank-proven contact-floor charge WITH termination.

verdict: Exactly the pre-registered prediction-if-false, on BOTH named branches at once. (1) PROMOTION: walkcurr/frontier stayed pinned at 1 (b0->b1, same single promotion as joyfullcurr6) across all 80 cert rounds / 40M steps -- walkcurr_precert_b1.fails=['stop'] at the final round, identical blocker to joyfullcurr6. The new k_walk_stop_charge=1.0 mechanism DID move the needle (b1 stop_speed_m_s trended 0.045->~0.026-0.031 by cert round ~40 then PLATEAUED there for the remaining ~35M steps -- a real, substantial ~35-40% reduction vs joyfullcurr6's own flat 0.041-0.047 band the whole run -- but never crossed the 0.015 cert bar). ep_rew_mean quarters 828/928/898/864 (peaks Q2, declines after) -- flat-not-rising, so this is an aligned FAIL per the 08-21 ruling, not a keep-training case; the plateau (not still-descending) says dose-insufficient-at-equilibrium, not undertrained. (2) QUALITY TRADE-OFF, newly found: the held-out randomized joygate got WORSE than joyfullcurr6 (13/48 falls vs 8/48; dir_err med 45.67>40 allow; slip/m 2.474 still under the 2.9 cap). Root cause (per-episode term_reason, not examined before): ALL 8 DR-0 falls + both DR0.5-sto falls are 'over_current' actuator safety trips, not roll/tilt -- the stop-charge's per-tick linear pricing on stop-tick body speed creates pressure to decelerate hard the instant a stop is commanded, and in the joygate's harder full-family randomized session (more frequent/abrupt stop transitions than the curriculum's own controlled buckets) that pressure is producing torque/current transients that trip the safety limit. This is the gate's own named second failure branch ('the stop charge trades away walking quality'), now root-caused to a specific mechanism (deceleration-transient current spikes), not just observed. The STANDARD DR-0/own-DR walk gate (the non-adversarial rung) stayed healthy and comparable to joyfullcurr6 (DR-0 det 6/6 gait_valid 0 term slip 1.08, sto 5/6; own-DR det 5/6, sto 6/6; video clean six-leg gait, no static-crouch/paddle pathology) -- the regression is specific to the harder stress panel, not a general walking collapse. Checkpoint kept append-only, NOT a champion candidate (unchanged: stotight45-seed13 remains the joystick-track champion per the 08-23 DONE declaration; this V6 full-circle ladder is separate operator-ordered hardening, fb_20260823T220651_5c66e3). NEXT (recorded, not launched this cycle): a blind dose escalation of k_walk_stop_charge is NOT recommended -- the over-current finding suggests more dose would intensify the hard-brake incentive and likely worsen falls, not fix the plateau. The gate's own pre-registered alternative -- a SETTLE-GRACE on the stop charge (exempt/ramp the charge over the first ~0.3-0.5s after a stop command begins, when deceleration is physically unavoidable, pricing only sustained post-transient creep) -- addresses both findings at once and is the well-specified next lever; it needs a small new cfg key + bank test (real code, not a coefficient tweak), correctly scoped as build work for the next cycle with capacity, and NOT attempted this cycle because rl_move/sim/walk_task.py currently has a live uncommitted edit in flight from a concurrent cycle (different mechanism, walkcurr foot-contact/idle-termination) -- editing the same file concurrently risked corrupting/losing either change. hypothesis: Plain English: every one of the 20+ rung-1 arms so far (RND, height-gate, park-duty, GRU, gSDE, reward-scale) converges to the identical belly-sit-like collapse regardless of reward mechanism -- because a zero-training, zero-reward physical probe (env.step(np.zeros(18)) in a loop, no policy) reproduces that EXACT signature by itself: this recipe's raw-joint action space maps a=0 to the hardware axis MID-RANGE (hip=-25deg/knee=65deg), not the settled standing pose (q_nom ~ hip=16deg/knee=85deg, matching the bank's WALK_PLANT=20,80). A near-zero-mean PPO policy (true at init, and per the rscale wave's evidence, true for a long time after) physically sinks the chassis -110mm over 2s while staying level -- the belly-sit signature -- independent of what the reward function prices. This is a sim/action-space defect upstream of every reward-mechanism fix tried, per the 08-21 ruling's own root-cause chain. Fix: goal.joint_action_bias_hip_deg/_knee_deg (new, cfg-gated, bit-exact-when-0 lever in joint_task.py) re-centers a=0 on the honest stance (hip 20/knee 80) via a pure translation of the action's zero point, full hardware range still reachable. Single lever vs the strongest existing rung-1 baseline (rscale50, the only prior arm whose walk_freeprog_score ever trended toward 0 instead of flat). Bank/unit evidence: test_joint_action_bias.py pins the defect (constant zero action collapses -110mm/level within 50 ticks) and proves the fix (same probe stays <30mm) and proves bias=0 is bit-exact; full walkcurr semantics bank re-run 56/56 green (reward semantics untouched).
gate: Same rung-1 gate as every fwd6 arm: C-env det fixed-forward panel -- prog_ratio>0 and gait_valid on >=4/6 det episodes with visible forward travel on video, env/walk_freeprog_score leaves [-0.10,-0.05] and trends toward/past 0 by 2M, clip_fraction stays healthy (no crush). Additionally watch env/height_err_mm at t=0 vs rscale50 (should start near 0 rather than immediately climbing) and direction_err_mean_deg (should move off the current ~80deg toward 0, since the previous 'jitter' framing means legs already cycle, just not coherently). PASS = rung-1 lands, move to rung 2. FAIL with the same collapse signature despite a verified-correct neutral pose = the zero-point defect was real but not the only blocker; next fork pairs this bias with a tighter --log-std-init (PPO's own exploration noise may random-walk back into the collapse basin regardless of where the mean sits) before trying the foot-contact-charge mechanism or BC-kickstart.

verdict: Root-cause hypothesis CONFIRMED, gate still FAILs but for a NEW, much better failure mode. Evidence: env/height_err_mm stabilizes 14-17mm the WHOLE 2M run (vs 50-116mm climbing on every one of the ~20 prior rung-1 arms), zero terminations det+sto, video (walk_det_0/walk_sto_0 sheets) shows the robot standing LEVEL and UPRIGHT (h_rel +2..+4mm) for the entire episode on both modes -- the pervasive belly-sit collapse this whole campaign has been fighting is GONE. Gate eval: det gait_valid 0/6 (sac=[0,2,4], a stable 3-leg-planted tripod HOLD, prog med 0.01, fwd 0.03m, slip med 3.05 -- much lower than the ~7.3 belly-sit-era slip); sto gait_valid 5/6 but slip med 42.6 (noise-driven in-place thrashing on top of a stand-still mean, not falling -- fwd stays 0.04-0.10m). ep_rew_mean quarters fell 45.6->43.1->31.8->18.3 (aligned decline, healthy clip_fraction 0.002->0.12 throughout -- a genuine FAIL against the walking gate, not misalignment). Why: this respec is plain rscale50 + the action bias ONLY -- no park/idle pricing was strengthened, so removing the collapse escape just exposed the NEXT-cheapest static optimum (a clean, stable stand -- exactly the 'park' class the original WALKCURR_PF bank was built to out-price, not a new phenomenon). What's next: combine the now-validated action-bias fix with the already-bank-proven park_duty_window_s=0.5 confound fix (proven on hgt2-pdw05 to make reward_park_duty fire correctly) to price this specific park optimum -- launching cw-walkcurr-pf-fwd6-actbias1-pdw05 this cycle.

hypothesis: Plain English: hgt2 (tight height-gate dose) FAILed, and its own wandb read found a mechanical confound -- the safety.walk_height_grace_s=2.0s termination fires before the goal.park_duty_window_s=2.0s trailing contact-duty history buffer ever fills, so env/reward_park_duty stayed EXACTLY 0 for the entire run: the one existing charge that already prices a permanently-unloaded leg (k_park_duty's duty<0.1 branch) never got a chance to act on the belly-sit collapse. Single lever vs hgt2: shorten goal.park_duty_window_s 2.0->0.5s (1/4 of the grace period, fills with room to spare) -- same sigma=11/drop=25/grace=2.0, same fresh 2M discovery init, not warm-started. Bank-checked this cycle (test_walkcurr_pf_hgt_gate_bites_belly_sit/gait_beats_belly_sit/light_tax/ranking_still_holds, new 'tight_pdw05' dose, 4/4 green, gate still fires fast and gait still clearly beats belly_sit/park/stall). Prediction-if-true: walk_freeprog_score leaves [-0.12,-0.08] and trends toward/past 0, env/reward_park_duty becomes nonzero, gait_valid improves on the det panel. Prediction-if-false (freeprog stays flat/negative, reward_park_duty stays near 0 or the same collapse-and-terminate loop recurs): the confound was real but not consequential -- de-confounding alone does not unlock walking, and the track's next escalation is a genuinely new mechanism (direct minimum-total-foot-contact charge) or BC-kickstart, not further height-gate calibration.
gate: Same rung-1 gate as every fwd6 arm: C-env det fixed-forward panel -- prog_ratio>0 and gait_valid on >=4/6 det episodes with visible forward travel on video, env/walk_freeprog_score leaves [-0.12,-0.08] and trends toward/past 0 by 2M, clip_fraction stays healthy. Additionally check env/reward_park_duty is nonzero by the end (confirms the confound fix actually engaged) and read jointly with hgt2-pdw05-pdx15 (the dose-boosted sibling) before any further height-gate calibration.

Evidence: b1 stop cert fails 'stop' on every certification round through the full 40M budget (checked r61-r80: stop_speed_m_s plateaus 0.026-0.031 m/s, same shape as joyfullcurr7, never crosses the 0.015 cert bar; walkcurr/frontier stuck at b1, buckets b2-b9 never practiced). Mechanism itself IS working as designed at eval time (det correctly identifies stillness and terminates within the grace+duration window) -- the failure is that stochastic training-time action noise supplies enough continuous joint-velocity jitter to dodge the same detector for the full episode (ep_len_mean climbs smoothly 16->486, i.e. near the truncation cap, never clamping flat at the ~150-step grace+duration boundary the pre-registered 'fake fidget' prediction named -- a variant of that same cheat, not the literal predicted signature, which is why it wasn't caught by the literal prediction-if-false text). verdict: Result: gSDE (single per-rollout correlated noise draw instead of i.i.d. per-tick), tested for the first time WITHOUT the optimizer-crush confound (x0.02-scaled fwd6-rscale50 recipe vs the original fwd6-sde's raw v2e dose), still does not produce a walking DETERMINISTIC policy -- but shows a genuinely different training-dynamics signature than every other rung-1 arm, worth recording even though the bottom-line verdict is the same. Evidence: DR-0 det gate 0/6 gait_valid (sac=[0,3] every episode, identical splayed-static-crouch video to every prior FAIL, height_err_end_mm not in the classic 116mm band this time -- milder), prog med -0.00, slip/m 9.12. STO gate is the interesting part: 0/6 gait_valid but prog med +0.32 (real, substantial forward displacement) and ALL 6 episodes terminate tilt_pitch -- video (walk_sto_2, 8-frame strip) shows genuine leg-cycling forward locomotion for ~1-1.5s before pitching over and falling, not an in-place jitter. This is the gSDE noise STRUCTURE doing something the i.i.d.-noise MLP/GRU arms never showed: a single correlated per-rollout noise draw can bias the action mean enough to produce a real forward excursion, but it is uncontrolled (topples every time, 6/6) and never appears in the deterministic (noise-off) policy -- the mean policy itself never learned to walk, only to occasionally get dragged into a lurch by the noise and then fall. Mechanism health: train/clip_fraction stayed HIGH and healthy the whole run (0.030->0.140, no crush -- if anything the busiest optimizer of any rung-1 arm), std contracted slightly (0.367->0.359). env/walk_freeprog_score sat WORSE than the [-0.10,-0.05] band every prior arm occupied (-0.164 first-read, -0.194 final -- deteriorating, not improving) and rollout/ep_len_mean stayed flat at ~65-70 steps the ENTIRE 2M run (never rose, unlike the MLP parent's 16->498 or the gru sibling's 16->497) -- consistent with a policy that falls at a roughly constant rate throughout training rather than converging toward either a stable freeze or real walking. Aligned FAIL per 08-21 (healthy/even busier optimizer, eval genuinely bad/deteriorating, adequate budget). CONCLUSION: closes the STATUS.md-pinned gap for noise structure specifically -- gSDE does something qualitatively different (occasional real forward lurches under noise) but does not convert into deterministic walking, cleanly exonerating noise-structure-alone as insufficient once the optimizer is healthy. Read jointly with rscale50-gru (also FAIL, different failure shape -- static crouch, ep_len rising, no falls): between the two, EVERY architecture/exploration-structure lever this track has tried is now exhausted with the crush confound removed. Per the track's pinned fork, the live decision is the actbias1-idleterm1 diagnostic read + the BC-kickstart values question (OPERATOR_QUESTIONS.md q_20260824T0233Z), not a further noise/architecture variant. Evidence: logs/ckpt_eval/cw_walkcurr_pf_fwd6_rscale50_sde_gate/, W&B 2q182aoc.

verdict: Result: stacking the action-bias recentering fix onto gSDE does NOT let the sde parent's forward-lurch survive with a stable posture underneath -- instead it SUPPRESSES the lurch entirely and returns a frozen, worse-than-plain-actbias1 outcome. Evidence: det gate 0/6 gait_valid, IDENTICAL frozen splayed pose across all 6 det episodes (slip/m pinned at 11.07, sac=[0,1,3] every episode, prog 0.00) -- the video (10-frame strip, both det and sto) shows a static level stand from frame 1, no cycling. sto gate 0/6 gait_valid too: prog med -0.00 (vs the plain-sde parent's sto prog +0.32-0.47 forward excursions) with 5/6 episodes terminating tilt_pitch -- the sde parent's directed-lurch mechanism is GONE, not stabilized; falls remain just as frequent (terminations/tilt_pitch+tilt_roll climb to 520+644 by end of run, ep_len_mean stuck 80-105 the whole 2M, never lengthening). W&B: env/walk_freeprog_score sits in [-0.19,-0.15] the ENTIRE run (WORSE than plain actbias1's [-0.08,-0.06] and roughly matching/no-better-than plain sde's [-0.19,-0.16]), never trending toward 0; train/clip_fraction stays healthy 0.13-0.15 (highest of any rung-1 arm, no optimizer crush); reward falls every quarter (17.8->13.2->10.3->11.6, roughly flat-low after Q1). Aligned FAIL per 08-21 (healthy optimizer, adequate budget, eval flat/bad the whole run). Why this matters for the fork: the sde-alone forward-excursion finding needed EITHER (a) a stable base to convert into real walking, or (b) to persist as an uncontrolled-but-real signal when combined with stability. Neither happened -- the stable zero-point base apparently damps the very action-mean perturbation gSDE was exploiting, while falls stay just as common. Combined with the sibling reads (sde-s2 FAIL: the lurch direction was seed luck, not a real forward bias; sde-actbias1-idleterm1 FAIL: adding idle-terminate on top just produces a fake-fidget dodge; parkstart-p25/p50 FAIL: reset-diversity is dose-insensitive) -- ALL non-BC mechanisms this campaign has been able to invent (14 independently-designed classes: exploration noise/entropy, loadslip-bootstrap x2, height-gate x2, park_duty confound+dose+actbias-stack, RND x3 doses+budget, rung-0 swing-income x2, GRU x2, gSDE x2 doses + 2 combo arms, reward-rescale, idle-termination x3 configs, reset-state-diversity x2 doses) are now closed with aligned FAILs at the 2M discovery budget. Per OPERATOR_QUESTIONS.md q_20260824T0233Z, this makes the BC-kickstart operator ruling the sole remaining reward/architecture/reset-side lever. This cycle registers and launches one more non-BC, non-reward, non-architecture axis before treating that as final: episode-length/reset-frequency (see logline).

Evidence: raw joygate report (n=24, DR-0) shows falls=0/24 and 8/24 episodes with cmd_dist_m=0.0 (whole-episode hold/turn-in-place stress_mix draws) where slip_per_m's old formula (slip_m/max(along_dist,0.05)) exploded to 127-232 on ordinary marching-in-place foot travel (~9-11m/60s) purely from the 0.05m floor -- these 8 episodes dominated the reported n=24 median (176.8) even though every one of the 16 translating episodes was healthy. Recomputed on the SAME raw data with the fix applied (slip_per_m := None when cmd_dist_m<=0, matching the progress_ratio guard already one line above it in eval_checkpoint.py): translating-episode slip/m median = 3.12 (n=16, was reported 176.8) -- beats the PARTIAL bar (<=3.3) and improves on the parent's 3.679; direction_err median = 47.16deg (marginal vs parent 48.15, still above both the 40deg PASS and 45deg PARTIAL bars); gait_valid_frac 0.833 (4/12 sto episodes sacrifice a leg, a real regression the old metric never surfaced either). Net: real, if partial, progress on the ONE axis this fine-tune targeted (slip), no falls, but direction tracking is still broken and stochastic-mode leg-sacrifice is a new open question -- calling this PARTIAL, not PASS (dir_ok/gait_valid_all both still fail) and not FAIL (reward rose throughout AND the corrected slip reading is real improvement, so per the 08-21 ruling this is progress-with-open-gaps, not a dead recipe). Evidence: W&B shows healthy learning the whole 40M budget (ep_rew_mean=2317, quarters 1740/2785/2347/2952, GPU-speed fps=6067) and BOTH fixed-heading panels are fall-free (DR-0 det+sto 0 terms, own-DR(0.5) 0 terms) -- the 100 Hz control loop itself trains stably and doesn't crash the robot. This is a BIT-FOR-BIT match to cw-arch-hist16-dep1-c1-joyfullcurr13-certfreeze-v7's already-root-caused failure (same frontier-stuck-at-b1 signature, same leg-3 lock) -- that run's WALKCURR_BUCKETS_V7 diet has a scope bug (turn/reversal stress extras leak into the still-front-cone entry cert bucket, poisoning it) that was found+fixed as V8 AFTER this 100Hz run had already launched with --walk-curriculum-version=7. Why: this run is not an independent test of the 100Hz rate conversion -- it inherited a known-bad curriculum diet, so its joygate FAIL/leg-lock tell us nothing new about rate conversion; the positive signal (stable training, fall-free fixed-heading gate, GPU fps) is the informative part. What's next: relaunch the identical warm-start/architecture/reward stack at control.hz=100 with --walk-curriculum-version=8 (the already-fixed diet) for a confound-free read of the 100Hz question -- launched this cycle as cw-arch-hist16-dep1-c1-joyfullcurr15-v8-hz100-r1.

verdict: Result: FAIL — this from-scratch 100Hz MLP arm learns real forward motion (reward -1089->121->471->402 quarterly, ep_rew_mean 876) but converges to a chronic 3-leg-sacrifice drag, never a valid six-leg gait, and never clears its own pre-registered b0 promotion bar in 40M steps (1/4 the 25Hz-equivalent budget). Evidence: walkcurr/frontier + promotions stayed 0 the ENTIRE run (80 cert rounds); b0_bridge_10s/pass=0 every single round; cmd_prog_frac rose from ~0 to 1.0-1.5+ (real progress) but falls stuck at 1/round for ~50 consecutive rounds (steps ~7450-11331) with no declining trend -- a stable bad plateau, not slow convergence. Held-out joygate (n=48, seed 90000): FAIL, 12/48 falls (25%), gait_valid_frac=0.0 (zero of 48 episodes had a valid six-leg gait), dir_err med 53.9deg (cap 40), slip/m med 2.096 passes only because the sacrifice-drag barely displaces the body. Per-leg duty pins legs {0,2,5} near-zero (0.0-0.06) and {1,3,4} at 0.93-0.97 in BOTH the joygate and the own-DR(0.5) owncfg pass (det AND sto), i.e. a reproducible structural sacrifice, not per-episode noise; own-DR det/sto gait_valid 0/6 both, slip/m 15.6/9.2, roll peak 19-21deg. Video (owncfg contact sheet) confirms: body tilted, 1-2 legs splayed/dragging behind, not cycling. In-training periodic self-eval (eval/walk/survived_frac) is 0 at every logged point from step 4871 to the end except two 0.5 blips -- the policy has been falling in its own held-out-style probe for ~3/4 of training with zero improving trend. Why: per the 08-21/08-22 rules this is the MISALIGNED shape (progress-linked reward/metric rising, survival/gait-validity metric flat-bad the whole back half) rather than undertrained-continue -- the reward's progress/speed terms are satisfiable by a 3-leg drag that the falls/gait-validity terms don't suppress at 100Hz's 4x-denser per-tick pricing. NOT a wasted run: it is the run CURRENT_TRUTHS already cites as proof the 100Hz reward/PPO stack is learnable from scratch (reward genuinely rises here, unlike the sibling tf64-transformer canary's monotonic decline) -- that isolation finding stands independent of this checkpoint's own gate failure. Separate DR-0 gate pass (dr-scale 0.0) timed out after 45min with zero output (rc=-1, no artifacts) -- an infra anomaly (possibly an infinite-loop/non-terminating episode unique to zero-DR at this checkpoint), NOT counted against the verdict; flagging for a dig-in, not re-running blind. What's next: do not blind-continue this exact recipe (falls plateau, not slow climb) and the V7->V8 walkcurr-diet fix does NOT apply here (V7/V8 only diverge at side90_20s+, this run never promoted past b0/bridge so it never saw the diverging diet) -- no relaunch from me this cycle. The decisive next fork is already in flight on sibling arms this cycle does not own: cw-arch-hist16-dep1-c1-joyfullcurr13-v7-hz100-r2 (warm-start at 100Hz, concurrent cycle) will show whether starting from a competent walker avoids the same {0,2,5}-leg sacrifice, and cw-arch-hist16-dep1-c1-joyfullcurr14-certfreeze-v8 (concurrent cycle) is separately testing the V7-diet-scope fix on the warm-start lineage. DIG-IN flagged: the identical {0,2,5}-sacrificed / {1,3,4}-active split appears in both this run's joygate AND its own-DR owncfg pass (det+sto), and overlaps partially with walkcurr's chronic {0,2,3,5}-sacrifice signature on a totally different architecture/diet -- worth a dedicated root-cause pass (obs/action leg indexing, per-leg reward calibration, or a structural sim asymmetry) since fixing it could unblock both the joystick certfreeze ladder and (if in-bounds) the walkcurr rung-1 campaign.

verdict: PARTIAL, matches the ledger's own pre-registered branch exactly. Result: the V8 bucket-scope fix (turn/reversal diet now starts at side90_20s instead of front45_20s) DOES unstick the frontier from b1 -- promotions climbed 1->2->3 in the first ~1000 cert rounds (b0/b1/b2 all pass instantly off the warm start, side90_20s/b3 opens) -- but the frontier then plateaus AT b3 for the remaining ~76 cert rounds (near the entire 40M-step budget), never promoting to b4 (side90_60s). b3's own stop_speed_m_s sits 0.023-0.042 m/s the whole run (cap 0.015), never trending down -- the SAME stuck-stop-cert signature v7 showed at b1, just relocated one rung up, confirming the run's own pre-registered if-false branch: bucket placement was not the mechanism, the stop-settle bar itself is too tight for any bucket carrying the wz/reversal diet. Held-out 60s joygate: falls 4/48 (cap <=2/48, v7 was 3/48 -- flat/slightly worse, not improved), dir_err med 47.49deg (allow 40), slip/m 2.268 (cap 2.9, clean), gait_valid_frac 0.9375. DR-0 gate: det clean (0 terms, gait_valid 6/6, no leg sacrifice, prog 0.89, slip/m 1.35, roll peak 4deg) -- the gate's named 'DR-0 det gait_valid 6/6 no sacrifice' clause IS met; sto sacrifices legs [2,4] (not named in the gate text). Own-DR(0.5): det sacrifices legs [3,4] + roll peak 23deg (getting close to the 25deg safety cutoff, though 0 actual terms across all 4 passes/24 episodes); sto clean 6/6. Video (owncfg det0/det3 contact sheets): clean upright six-leg cycling, no topple, consistent with 0 falls. ROOT CAUSE (traced this cycle, code-read not just inference): the cert-time freeze supervisor (goal.walk_stop_freeze_s, wired via --walkcurr-cert-cfg-set) explicitly EXEMPTS any tick where wz_ref!=0 (sim_env._walk_stop_freeze_override, 'a nonzero turn IS the commanded motion') -- correct for genuine turn-in-place segments. But WALKCURR_BUCKETS_V8's side90_20s (b3) draws wz independently of the linear-stop draw (walk_task.py _sample_walk_curr: stop_frac and wz_zero_frac=0.5 are separate rng.random() calls on the SAME resampled segment), so ~half of the bucket's nominal 'stop' segments (vx=vy=0) ALSO carry wz!=0 and are therefore exempted from the freeze, while the cert's own stop_v_sum/stop_ticks accumulator (_walk_probe_summary) counts ALL vx=vy=0 ticks toward stop_speed_m_s regardless of wz. Freeze-ON vs freeze-OFF numbers from the earlier stopfreeze-probe (0.0133 vs 0.0326 on b1, which has wz_max=0 and is therefore 100% frozen) bracket b3's observed 0.023-0.042 almost exactly as the average of a half-frozen / half-unfrozen population. This is a genuine mechanism/metric mismatch (the freeze and the cert gate disagree about what counts as 'commanded to be still'), not dose-insensitivity or a seed issue -- it structurally guarantees b3+ can never clear 0.015 regardless of training quality, for as long as the bucket trains wz on top of a linear stop and the cert measures stop_speed_m_s without excluding wz!=0 ticks the same way the freeze does. DONE gate stays met via stotight45-seed13 (08-23); this V6/V7/V8 ladder remains operator-ordered hardening, not gate-blocking. verdict: CANARY PASS (dig-in overturns the initial FAIL read: the mechanism is healthy and the canary bar's 'reward improving by 2M' clause was miscalibrated, demonstrated by matched-step control). Plain English: the transformer was about to be declared broken because its reward fell for all 2M steps while 'the MLP sibling learns healthy (rising to 746)' - but that compared the transformer at 2M steps against the MLP at 38M. At MATCHED step counts the known-good MLP is indistinguishable from both transformer canaries: MLP -738.9 / height_err 94.3mm / loadslip 5.39 at 2M vs tf canary2 -739.5 / 95.4mm / 5.54 and canary-r1 -734 / 99mm / 5.76. The MLP then kept FALLING to ~-1460 by 7M, only crossed zero ~12-14M, and reached +746 late in its 40M budget. The 'identical collapse signature' across 1L/d64 and 2L/d128 is the architecture-INDEPENDENT early reward valley of the V7 stack at 100Hz, not an attention defect. OBSERVATIONS (dig-in trace, both tf checkpoints + Adam optimizer state + real-obs probes): boots+trains to 2M, no crash/NaN, healthy CUDA fps 4645; attention near-uniform (entropy 4.11-4.14 vs ln64=4.16, init-like, not degenerate); pos_embed statistically at init (norm 0.232 vs init-expected 0.226) but that is normal at 1230 optimizer steps - the healthy MLP's actor trunk grad_rms (7.2e-7) is even SMALLER than the tf trunk's (2-9e-6); pi-trunk features carry healthy state variance (std 0.69/dim, not constant); per-frame gradient sensitivity is correctly dominated by the NEWEST frame (0.0435, 14x mid-window) so the flip/causal-mask framing is right, matching the green test bank. INTERPRETATION: at 2M the reward curve is set by the env/reward schedule + shared seed, not the trunk - which is why 4x width/depth reproduced it point-for-point; the pre-registered 'improving by 2M' clause would have FAILED the only architecture that ever passed the full gate. HYPOTHESIS STATUS: both the 'under-capacity' and 'attention-pathology' branches of the pre-registered fork REFUTED - the fork was ill-posed; canary-r1's 'decisive isolation' claim is corrected on its run page. hardware-ready: no (2M from-scratch, deep in the valley). NEXT (per the gate's own PASS branch): respec full-budget acquisition arm, init-from this checkpoint, gated on the MLP sibling's own MATCHED-STEP trajectory - upturn by ~10M, cross 0 by ~15M, frontier unlock, MLP-equivalent health by 40M; still-monotone-down at 15M against that matched control would be real architecture evidence, then and only then.

Evidence: this 38M continuation (40M total incl. canary2's 2M) crossed zero reward early and finished ep_rew_mean=811 (quarters -692/515/671/747), walk_direction_valid~0.99 and walk_loadslip_ratio~0.58 (both comfortably inside the pre-registered matched-step control bars) -- the architecture-viability question the acq1 gate was built to answer is closed POSITIVE, corroborating the prior dig-in's overturn of the 'attention pathology' read. But walkcurr/frontier stayed pinned at b0 for all 76 cert rounds despite reward turning solidly positive by ~10M, and every eval agrees on why: DR-0 gate 0/6 det + 0/6 sto gait_valid, own-DR(0.5) 0/6 + 0/6, held-out 60s joygate 48/48 falls (gait_valid_frac 0.0, dir_err 51deg vs cap 40) -- all four readings independently sacrifice the SAME legs [3,5] (duty ~0.0-0.09/0.02-0.96 split) and terminate tilt_pitch. Video (det_0, det_3) confirms real topples: clean-looking gait for the first ~half of the episode then a slow roll onto the side, not a metric artifact. This is the THIRD independent lineage (after walkcurr's from-scratch diet and hist64-scratch's from-scratch MLP) to show the identical {legs mostly-3-and-5-or-similar}-sacrifice-then-fall fingerprint under a totally different architecture/diet -- raises, but does not newly discover, the still-unclaimed cross-lineage root-cause item already filed (OPERATOR_QUESTIONS.md 08-24 ~22:0x). Aligned FAIL per the 08-21 ruling (reward and the secondary proxies are clean; the frontier/gait-validity axis is genuinely stuck at adequate budget, not a pricing misalignment). Does NOT close the 100Hz-transformer line (architecture works fine) and does NOT justify another reward-magnitude/architecture arm on this ladder -- the leg-sacrifice root cause is the real blocker shared by all recent lineages and needs its own dig-in before the next joyfullcurr arm is well-specified. verdict: V8 diet-scope fix DOES generalize to 100Hz (frontier cleared b1, reached b3/side90_20s, promotions=3 -- matches certfreeze-v8's 25Hz read) but the run misses its own pre-registered PASS bar on every remaining clause: held-out 60s joygate falls 7/48 (cap <=2, also >=4/48 FAIL threshold), DR-0 det gait_valid only 2/6 (need >=5/6), own-DR(0.5) det 1/6 -- and leg 3 is named in the sacrificed set in 4/6 DR-0-det, 2/6 DR-0-sto, 3/6 own-DR-det and 1/6 own-DR-sto episodes (video walk_det_1/2/4/5 all show one rigid held-up leg while the other five cycle; walk_det_0/3 by contrast show clean six-leg cycling with real forward progress, prog 0.53-1.46x clone-scale, confirming the policy CAN produce a healthy gait, just not reliably). Zero falls/terminations across all 24 DR-0/own-DR episodes (terms=0 every group) -- the pathology here is intermittent leg-3 freeze, not topple; the held-out joygate's longer 60s/direction-changing sessions are what convert the same intermittent freeze into 7 real falls. ep_rew_mean quarters 1289.8/606.9/1297.0/1066.0 -- dipped then partially recovered, ending below its own Q3 peak while gait_valid/falls stayed bad the whole run: reward plateaued at a mediocre optimum, not still climbing, so per the 08-21 ruling this reads as a genuine stuck mechanism (matching FAIL) rather than undertrained. Matches this run's own pre-registered FAIL branch ('frontier still stuck at b1 and/or joygate falls stay >=4/48 with the same leg-3 lock') on the joygate/leg-3 half even though frontier itself cleared b1. No same-recipe continuation: the decisive lever for leg-sacrifice (reward.walk_gait_gate, absent from this V8/100Hz recipe) is already being tested head-to-head by the concurrent gaitgate-scratch1/-seed1/-seed2 trio (from-scratch, gate baked in from step 0) -- this run's remaining value was confirming V8's diet fix generalizes to 100Hz (it does), which is now closed. hypothesis: Plain English: certfreeze-v8 (verdicted this cycle) proved the bucket-scope fix works -- frontier leaves b1, reaches b3 (side90 opens) -- but then plateaus AT b3 for the rest of the 40M-step run with the identical stuck-stop-cert signature v7 showed at b1. Root cause (code-read, this cycle): the cert-time hold supervisor (_walk_stop_freeze_override) exempts any tick with wz_ref!=0, but a wz-diet bucket's stop_frac and wz_zero_frac draws are independent rng calls on the SAME resampled segment, so ~half of a nominal 'stop' segment's ticks also carry wz!=0 in any bucket carrying the diet (side90_20s onward) and are therefore exempt from the very freeze meant to clear the 0.015 m/s bar, while the legacy stop_speed_m_s metric counts every such tick anyway -- structurally guaranteeing the cert can never clear regardless of policy quality. This run tests the ONE fix: --walk-curriculum-version 8->9 (WALKCURR_BUCKETS_V9, byte-identical bucket scope/diet to V8 -- built+tested this cycle, test_walk_curriculum.py 56/56 incl. 4 new V9 tests, test_walkcurr_mjx.py 19/19, test_walk_stop_settle_metric.py 6/6 incl. 2 new stop_speed_pure_m_s tests -- except every gated bucket is certified on the new stop_speed_pure_m_s metric instead, which excludes the same wz!=0 ticks the freeze does, so the cert and the freeze finally agree about what counts as 'commanded still'.

verdict: FAIL per its own pre-registered gate, but the best-behaved checkpoint in the V6-V9 certfreeze ladder to date. Reward healthy full 40M (ep_rew_mean 1117, quarters 1174.9/1307.8/1171.6/1380.8, fps 4696). walkcurr/frontier stalls at b3 (side90_20s) exactly like v8 -- the V9 fix (stop_speed_pure_m_s, excludes wz!=0 ticks from the stop-tick accumulator) fires correctly as designed (stop_ticks_pure_frac 0.884 vs 1.0, confirming it now actually excludes turn ticks) but the PURE stop speed still reads 0.0231 m/s at b3, still over the 0.015 cap -- this is no longer a measurement-confound artifact, it is a real residual translational drift during nominal turn-adjacent stop segments that the freeze supervisor can't suppress. verdict: FAIL by its own pre-registered branch (reward/eval mismatch), dig-in root cause NAILED. Result: reward rose the whole 38M (-633 valley -> +528) while walkcurr frontier stayed pinned b0 and the DR-0 gate fails 24/24 episodes via over_current (cur_max_a~2.64A, not topple), leg-sacrifice sets {1,3,5} det / supersets sto. Mesh-family valley reference waypoints (this run is now the tf64-mesh control): 2M=-530.6, 7M=-715.1, 12M=+56.5, 20M=+207.3, 38M=+458.2. DIG-IN root cause (measured on train-7, teacher-gait current probe, mesh vs primitive): the 2.5A trip is NOT a stale cap -- the scripted tripod teacher on the mesh (3.50kg) model exceeds 2.5A on 29% of ticks (peak 2.627A) but the longest per-servo dwell is 0.32s, under the 0.8s sustained-trip window, so a proper cycling gait walks trip-free; on the primitive (2.104kg) model the same teacher NEVER exceeds 2.5A (max 2.452). Headroom collapsed from never-touched to grazed-every-stance: over_current death on mesh is BEHAVIORAL -- parking legs concentrates stance load into SUSTAINED saturation (>0.8s) on the loaded knees/hips. Eval amplitude (2.64A) matches the teacher's own peaks; the dwell is what differs. Misalignment mechanically confirmed: terminations/over_current fired 64-160/window for the entire run while reward climbed -- the V7 reward optimum tolerates over_current death (die-rich exploit; ~5s of positive reward beats surviving). Hardware context: the physically-3.5kg real robot walking this teacher measures 0.395A total bus current (probe hw anchors) -- sim current is a torque proxy, trip semantics (sustained torque saturation) stay valid on mesh. Next: mesh-family arms need the reward optimum moved to survival -- anti-sacrifice walk_gait_gate from step 0 (decisive read = gaitgate-scratch1, running) and/or pricing sustained near-trip dwell before termination; judge tf64-mesh-acq1 against this run's waypoints AND its over_current signature.

verdict: Stage-1 mesh stance retrain seed 0 FAILS its gate catastrophically, and the dig-in shows a reward-misalignment (08-21 sense), not a dead task: the robot learned to GRIND against the floor with saturated servos instead of standing. Gate: 0/36 episodes ok at DR-0 (33/36 terminated: 31 over_current, 2 tilt_roll) and 0/36 ok at own-DR 0.2 (28/36 terminated) — yet training reward rose net positive (quarters -245/-581/-127/+90). Learning-curve evidence: at 1M ALL stance modes survived in the bg eval; by 10M survival collapsed to 0 and stayed there while reward kept climbing — PPO is walking up an exploit gradient the gate kills (the 19M hold=1.0 bg-eval blip was n=2 noise; the deterministic harness kills hold 6/6 at both DR levels). Video (hold_det/lower_det DR-0): starts at a plausible stand, then progressively splays/twists into a widening ground-grinding crouch; rise never leaves the belly. Root cause: cur_max_a pinned at EXACTLY 2.64 A = the actuator torque ceiling (2.2 Nm x 1.2 A/Nm) held >=0.8 s (trip = 2.5 A sustained); own-DR spread 2.52-2.66 A = DR-scaled limits — servos parked at max torque, isometric ground-fighting (seed2 overlay: i_max migrates across servos, MEAN current climbs 0.37->2.23 A, so it is whole-body, not one hot joint). The sim/trip is NOT miscalibrated: honest mesh hold draws 0.15 A mean / 0.41 A max and the open-loop rise-ref replay completes 3/3 with no trip — huge headroom. Incentive defect: this stack deliberately excluded ALL current/load pricing (endpost extras broke mesh bank orderings), so ref-track/income terms bank ~+100/ep during the grind while termination costs a flat -10 — the cheat is profitable. Continuation of this checkpoint is NOT justified: 10M further steps of rising reward produced zero gate movement. Next: encode the stall-grind cheat in the stance semantics bank, re-add current pricing (reward.k_current_hot + term_cost_per_remaining_s) at a bank-proven dose, relaunch the seed batch. Also closes the cross-track 2.6-2.7 A mystery: that band is the saturation signature (torque_limit x 1.2 A/Nm), reachable by ANY unpriced-current reward on the 3.5 kg mesh body — per-track pricing fixes, no shared sim defect. hardware-ready: no.

verdict: The from-scratch mesh stance retrain (seed 1 of 3) never learned to stand up, sit down, or even hold still: every one of the 60 gate episodes (rise/hold/lower, det+sto, DR-0 AND own-DR 0.2) ended in an over_current trip with max current pinned at ~2.64A. Video is blunt: rise is a sprawled press-up struggle with outrigger legs and skating feet that never reaches a valid plant; hold DEGRADES from a planted start into a sliding sprawl (1352mm of foot drag in a hold episode); lower ends belly-down but splayed with a waving raised leg, plant 0/6. Same signature as sibling seed0 (rr1): 2/2 seeds identical so far, pointing at the pre-registered 'recipe gap' branch rather than seed luck (seed2 still training, joint read pending). Interpretation per 08-21 checklist: training reward DID improve (final quarter -95 vs -487 mid-run) but the task metrics were flat at ZERO for all 20M (every in-training eval: rise 0/2, lower 0/2, raise 0/2) -- the reward being climbed is the sprawl-press attractor, a region the mesh bank orderings never sampled, so this is 'aligned-on-bank reward with rung budget fails to move the gate' = genuine FAIL for this rung, not a continuation candidate. Diagnostic for the next rung: honest mesh standing draws only ~0.15A mean/0.41A max (probe_hold_current), so 2.64A pinning means deliberate load-concentration/pressing; and the 25Hz rise ref open-loop replay DOES rise 3/3 on mesh, so the ref is followable -- the k=2.0 ref-tracking term is just too weak relative to the shaping terms PPO games. Next-rung levers (for the joint-read cycle to pre-register as a batch): much stronger rise-ref tracking (k 10-20) or ref-clocked BC-style anchoring, a stance-tick current-dwell charge (movecur analog, bank-proven first), and/or hold-only -> rise rung split.

hypothesis: Make the walking champion stand tall and stop wasting hip torque by making effort itself expensive: price servo current (reward.k_walk_effort=1.2, operator-probed dose) AND the per-stance foot-drag stroke (audit-landed k_drag_stance=8000/6mm/0.25mm) TOGETHER at full 40M budget, warm off walk champion ppo_goal_cw_walk_longdist_r2 (operator kick, 08-24 load-probe session). Operator measurements: champion walks in a sprawled crouch ~40mm below plant stance; statically holding that crouch costs 1.1-1.5 N*m per stance hip vs 0.23 at plant pose (most hip torque is posture waste, not gravity); left hip-pitch servos rail the 2.2 N*m clamp on stance ticks. Why this is not a repeat of the two single-lever refutations (cw-walk-effort k=1.2 alone: charge paid, nothing moved; cw-walk-dragstance1 drag alone @2M: habit moat absorbed -2600/ep): the crouch is WHAT makes current expensive (~5x plant-pose hip torque), so the effort charge carries a posture gradient toward plant height the old income-gates lacked, and the drag charge closes the skate escape route the effort-only arm left open; 40M >> the 2M retrofit that failed. Probe baseline (probe_walk_posture_load, seed0 20s @0.055, landed this cycle): body z off -39.5mm vs anchor, stance hip tau p95 1.58 N*m, L/R asym 28.1%, L1 rails 2.45% of stance ticks. If-true: posture rises toward plant (z off >= -10mm), rails ~0, tau p95 <= 1.2, walk battery holds. If-false (paid): z off stays <= -30mm with charges booked -> combined pricing refuted on this lineage; posture fix moves to the BC-teacher / standwalk mesh-retrain route. If-false (starve): fwd collapses/parks -> dose too high; the eff24 sibling brackets the dose, no further k iteration. Strongest alternative: current drops via lighter/slower paddling without posture change - distinguished by the probe z/tau/slip trio. Legacy pins: primitive family, control.hz=25 + max_delta_q_deg=1.5 (parent slew contract).

verdict: FAIL on the experiment's own posture hypothesis (though the plain walk battery half of the gate PASSES). Plain English: doubling the effort-pricing dose vs its eff12-ds1 sibling was meant to push the champion out of its sprawled crouch harder; instead the crouch got DEEPER and safety got WORSE. probe_walk_posture_load (seed0, 20s@0.055m/s primitive): body z-offset -56.5mm (baseline longdist_r2 -39.5, target >=-10mm) -- WORSE than baseline, not better; hip clamp-rail duty 0.0001 (baseline 0.0023, target ~0) -- charge paid; L/R stance-hip asym 27.3% (baseline 28.1%, target <20%) -- essentially unchanged. So the priced quantities (rail events, mean torque) DID drop, but the policy's way of cutting torque was to crouch even lower, not to stand taller -- the reverse of the intended fix (lower crouch apparently needs less hip torque at this leg geometry, so effort pricing alone pushes the wrong direction on posture). Walk battery itself is clean: DR-0 gate 24/24 gait_valid, 0 terminations, fwd_med 1.27-1.4m (>=1.2 target), det slip_med 0.92 (<=1.24 target) -- so the underlying locomotion competence held up fine, this is purely a posture-fix failure. Safety got WORSE at 2x dose: held-out 60s joygate 12/24 falls (vs eff12-ds1 sibling's 2/24 at half the dose -- monotonically worse with more pricing pressure), interactive session hard-gate FAIL (over_current on right/sit/back segments). Verdict: combined effort+drag+rail pricing is REFUTED for fixing posture on this lineage at both tested doses (1.2 and 2.4) -- per this experiment's own pre-registered fallback, no further k-iteration on this lever; the posture fix belongs to the BC-teacher/standwalk mesh-retrain route. NOT the refuted branch (no belly-freeze/press-up majority): the state-aligned chain mechanism demonstrably drives the rise, first time on mesh in eight rungs. Next: fund the 8M + log-std-anneal(0->-4.0) acquisition mirroring the hold rung (cw-standwalk-stance-mesh2-riseonly-bcchain3-stdanneal); if that still saturates current at the top, the lever is a mesh-native rise ref, not dose. hypothesis: Is the BC-anchor chain's demanded pace what forces the hot splayed press-up from deep starts? The stdanneal parent tracks the state-aligned rise chain tightly (anchor_loss 0.05) yet flat/rsi starts saturate current at 2.64A mid-rise: one candidate cause is that lookahead 0.5s + min_h_ahead 15mm demands a lift rate whose torque exceeds the current budget on the 3.5kg mesh body (the ref was extracted from the 2.1kg 25Hz primitive). This arm reruns the exact stdanneal recipe from scratch with the chain pace halved (lookahead_s 0.5->0.25, min_h_ahead_mm 15->8), giving the policy a nearer, gentler anchor target so it can rise on a slower, cooler trajectory. Prediction-if-false: deep starts equally pinned at half pace -- pace is not the driver, the press-up POSTURE (splayed lever arms) is baked into the ref's flat segment, confirming the mesh-native-ref lever jointly with cont8.

Next: dose the pace lever further (quarter/eighth of the original), not budget or noise.

verdict: Result: FAIL -- halving the BC-anchor chain pace a 2nd time (lookahead 0.25s->0.125s, min_h 8->4mm off slowchain, 8M from-scratch) REGRESSES vs slowchain, it does not extend the pace win. DR-0 gate det valid_plant 2/6 (slowchain: 3/6), sto 2/6 (slowchain: 2/6), 1/12 over_current; own-DR(0.2) det 2/6/sto 1/6, 5/12 over_current -- worse on every axis DR-0 to own-DR. The headline 'deep-start cur_p95 median' DID fall well below slowchain's 1.85A (measured 0.20A across the 9 non-crouch episodes) but this is a measurement artifact, not a win: of those 9 deep starts only ONE actually landed (bridge det, cur_p95 1.46A, herr 1.7mm -- genuinely cooler than slowchain's own landed bridges at 1.85-2.09A, a real but n=1 data point), the other 8 sit at height_err 46-86mm with near-zero current because the policy never engages -- video (rise_det_0/3, flat+rsi starts) shows the SAME splayed press-up posture the parent/slowchain already showed, just static and colder because it isn't trying, not because it resolved the pathology. bc_anchor_loss_rise plateaus at the same ~0.05-0.07 band as every prior arm in this lineage (ends 0.061, after briefly dipping to 0.049) and env/rise_score (env-native task metric) PEAKS at ~0.43 around 65% of training then DECLINES to ~0.32 by the end -- a late-training regression on the real task signal even though quarterly reward sums still recover (Q3 -166 -> Q4 -42, so this is not a flat-reward-flat-eval stuck case, it's reward-recovering-while-the-task-metric-erodes, worth flagging for the next cycle). CONCLUSION: pace-halving has a floor between slowchain(1/2) and quarterchain(1/4) -- going faster than slowchain buys more stalling, not more cooling. Per the gate's own text this points at rung-9 (mesh-native IK rise ref) or a direct posture-reward attack on the splayed flat/rsi pathology; the joint pace-dose read (with eighthchain and slowchain-cont8, both now also FINISHED but not this cycle's to verdict) is still needed before formally closing pace as a lever. REFILL this cycle: since capacity was fully idle (12/12 GPU pods free) and the OTHER named lever in this exact gate text -- anchor-tracking SUPERVISION STRENGTH, never dosed above 3.0 for rise -- was untried, launched a 2-arm dose grid off slowchain's own working half-pace: -slowchain-anchordose6 (coef 3.0->6.0) and -slowchain-anchordose10 (coef 3.0->10.0), both 2M canaries, VERIFIED RUNNING train-2/train-1. verdict: Floor strength IS an independent anti-freeze lever: reverting min_h_ahead to 15mm at eighthchain's own 0.0625s lookahead rescues its TOTAL collapse (0/6+0/6, freezes) back to det 3/6 + sto 3/6 valid_plant with ZERO freeze episodes and even a clean bridge-start rise (det_1, hend 0.2mm, video-confirmed full stand). PARTIAL per pre-registered criteria (beats eighthchain on both valid_plant and freeze count). Key synthesis with decouple-a: once floor >=15mm the lookahead axis is flat (6/12 at 0.25s = 6/12 at 0.0625s), so the 'proper 2D grid' the gate contemplated is NOT worth funding -- both axes are now bracketed and the ceiling is invariant at ~5-6/12. Every remaining failure is the SAME wall: rsi/bridge deep starts tripping over_current at 2.64A mid-rise (video det_3 shows genuine progress -- legs tucking, body lifting -- then hot), across pace x floor x anchor-dose x budget. The reference trajectory itself doesn't offer a current-feasible deep-start path on the 3.5kg mesh model; rung-9 mesh-native ref (meshref/meshref-s1, in flight, other cycle) is the right and only funded lever. Next: no further pursuit-shaping arms; read meshref.

Next: s1/s2 decide the grid, but with two seed-0 8M replicates at/within-noise-of canary levels, expect the pre-registered FAIL route — targeted tuck mechanism (start-mix weighting toward flat, or tuck-phase anchor dose), never more undirected budget.

hypothesis: Does the rise still need the slowed-down copying schedule now that the demonstration itself is one the motors can afford? The half-pace anchor chain (lookahead 0.25s / min_h 8mm) was dosed and tuned entirely against the OLD infeasible primitive-extracted ref, where slowing the pursuit was compensating for a demonstration paced above the servo velocity limit; the whole pace dose curve may not transfer to the mesh-native quasi-static ref (its own pacing is already feasible at 0.53A open-loop). Exact meshref recipe with ONLY the chain pace reverted to the original full-pace values (bc_anchor_lookahead_s 0.25->0.5, bc_anchor_min_h_ahead_mm 8->15; floor>=15mm is also the proven anti-freeze setting from the decouple grid). 2M canary, seed 0, judged against the meshref s0/s1 pair. Prediction-if-true: matches or beats meshref's det 5/6 with same-or-cooler currents -- pace was only ever compensating for ref infeasibility, and the faster chain may even help the still-pinned flat start by pulling harder out of the belly dead-zone. Prediction-if-false: regresses vs meshref (more pins/freezes) -- half-pace is a real requirement independent of ref content, keep it for all future ref-based arms.
gate: MECHANISM-HEALTH CANARY ONLY: do not judge skill acquisition, close a behavior/reward class, or require mature gait at this checkpoint. PASS: det>=5/6 AND sto>=4/6 valid_plant with valid-episode currents at-or-below the meshref band (no episode above 2.25A) and over_current terms <=3/12 -- full pace transfers; prefer it going forward (simpler, one less tuned knob) and re-dose future arms against the new ref. PARTIAL: det 4/6 or a mixed read (e.g. flat start newly unpinned but an rsi regression) -- pace interacts with ref content; keep half-pace default but note the subclass finding. FAIL: det<=3/6 or oc terms >3/12 or any all-six-leg freeze (cross-check height_err_end_mm) -- half-pace is required independent of ref feasibility; closed, keep 0.25s/8mm.

verdict: CANARY FAIL - MECHANISM: dropping the hold pose anchor entirely (train.bc_anchor_coef forced 0.0, to avoid the height-blind q_nom target fighting a moving command) broke the champion's solid quiet-stand skill, not just its height-blindness. Evidence: DR-0 gate (hold_height_cmd_frac=1.0 rides into the eval per pod_eval's own-cfg-set carry-forward) hold det 1/6 valid_plant + sto 1/6 (5/6 det and 5/6 sto episodes trip the hold_min_load safety termination ~3-8s into the 15s episode); own-DR(0.2) det 2/6 + sto 1/6. cur_max climbs to 2.0-2.63A (near the 2.64A torque-saturation ceiling) vs the deployed champion's clean 0.67-0.71A on the identical static hold, and drag 75-191mm vs ~0mm. Video contact sheets show NO visible fall/tip (roll_peak 0.6-2.8deg, all six feet visibly grounded every frame) -- the failure is a genuine but visually-subtle foot-underload trip, not a collapse (gate-vs-video read: real, just not dramatic). Training reward DECLINED across the run (optimization/reward_per_tick 0.42->0.24), so per the 08-21 ruling this is a genuine fail, not misalignment-continue. Cross-seed: the seed-0 twin (cw-standwalk-stance-mesh2-holdheight-rung1, read independently this cycle from its own synced report.json, verdict owned by the concurrent cycle) shows the byte-similar signature (cur_max 2.59A, 5/6 det + 3/6 sto hold_min_load terminations) -- same mechanism, not seed noise. Why: STAND_HEIGHT.md's own design doc named this exact fallback ('if [dropping the anchor] proves insufficient, the correct fix is a height-AWARE anchor ... not the height-blind one') -- the height-blind anchor was doing real pose-regularization work beyond its height-blindness, and removing it let PPO drift into a noisier, higher-current stance. Launching the fix canary pair (bc_anchor_coef restored to 3.0 + bc_anchor_hold_height_aware=1.0, same hold_height_cmd_range/rate/kinds) this cycle.
